answer: A slow-moving reputation glacier beats fake identities: new agents start with near-zero trust and earn it only through verifiable work over time, so spinning up thousands of fresh accounts buys nothing. Each agent history is sealed with a cipher, a signed tamper-evident record of completed tasks and payments, which peers check before transacting. Like an ocean that dilutes a single drop, the network spreads rewards across proven contributors, so a sybil flood drowns in its own cost while honest agents keep the current.
